Door of the Sheep
dôr ŭv thē shēp
n. / title (Christ as the only lawful entrance to the fold and to salvation; rendering Greek he thura ton probaton)
Door, Old English duru; Greek thura. In an eastern sheepfold the shepherd often lay across the opening at night, so that the door was a body.

See also: Door of the Sheep

Biblical Definition

“Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep” (John 10:7); “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture” (John 10:9). He contrasts every other approach: “He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber” (John 10:1). The exclusivity is repeated four chapters later — “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” (John 14:6) — and by Peter before the council: “neither is there salvation in any other” (Act 4:12).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines door as an opening or passage into a house or apartment; the frame of boards that shuts such an opening; and, figuratively, entrance, means of approach or access.

expand to see more

DOOR, n. An opening or passage into a house, or other building, or into any room, apartment or closet, by which persons enter.

2. The frame of boards, or any piece of board or plank that shuts such an opening.

3. Entrance; as the door of life.

4. Avenue; means of approach or access.

Key Scripture

John 10:7 — "Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep."

John 10:9 — "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture."

John 10:1 — "Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber."

John 14:6 — "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

Act 4:12 — "Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved."

Modern Corruption

Many doors are proposed and Christ called Himself the door, with everyone climbing in another way a thief.

expand to see more

“I am the door” is one of the least negotiable sentences in Scripture, because a door is not a preference among routes; it is the opening in a wall, and where there is one door there is no second. The Lord makes the exclusion explicit rather than leaving it to inference: he that entereth not by the door, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. The alternatives are not described as sincere paths up the same mountain but as burglary. That is offensive in every age and was designed to be.

The corruption in the church is subtler than pluralism and more common: additional doors of its own manufacture — a rite, a party, an experience, a standard of respectability, without which a man is not quite let in. Every such requirement is a second entrance cut in a wall that has one, and John 10:9 is the answer to it: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved. Any man, and the only qualification named is entering.

The second half of the promise is usually dropped and is the tender part: he shall go in and out, and find pasture. The door is not a turnstile admitting a man once to a locked enclosure; it is the ordinary movement of a flock, out to feed in the morning and in to safety at night, both directions through the same Person. Salvation in this figure is not merely getting in. It is a life with a door in it that is always open the right way.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek thura (G2374), door; aule (G833), fold, court; sozo (G4982), to save; nome (G3542), pasture; lestes (G3027), robber.

expand to see more

Greek thura (G2374) — door; John 10:1, 10:2, 10:7, 10:9, Revelation 3:20, 4:1.

Greek aule (G833) — sheepfold, court; John 10:1, 10:16.

Greek nome (G3542) — pasture; John 10:9, and 2 Timothy 2:17 of a canker spreading.

Usage

"“I am the door of the sheep” — an opening in a wall, and there is one."

"“Climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief” — the alternatives named as burglary."

"“Shall go in and out, and find pasture” — the half that is usually dropped."
